$comment: READ-ONLY. Answers one question before a column is attached to a governed
element: has the catalogue declared this object unfit to use?
WHY THIS EXISTS. Measured 2026-09-08 on gartner2026.mtse, N=5: every run of
cde_creator attached at least one table the catalogue had declared do-not-use —
four reached for a `tmp_` working copy, one for a retired annual archive, each
with sound-looking reasoning about lineage completeness. The prompt tells the
agent to attach an element at every layer it exists in, and nothing outranked
that. A retired copy is not an upstream layer, it is a parallel one.
WHY A TOOL RATHER THAN A PROMPT RULE. The first fix was prose: 'exclude any
table the catalogue declares unfit, and read the containing table's description
for the declaration.' It passed its validation run and was reverted anyway —
the agent had excluded on the `tmp_` NAME PREFIX, never reading any
declaration. Right answer, wrong mechanism, and a name heuristic would not have
caught `legacy.customer_exposure_2023`. Noah's call, and it is the right one:
asking a model to infer a governance rule from a sentence is the wrong move in
a product whose entire purpose is structured metadata. A trust flag is a typed
field with a mandatory reason. There is nothing to infer.
BUILT, NOT CAPTURED. gartner2026 already carries a custom tool named
`Get Table Trust Flags` (function_name get_table_flags_dp, id c8ceef74) that
someone else built. It is not ours, not in this repo, and will not exist on the
next tenant. This one is written from the published Trust Check Flags API so
the solution owns its own dependency.
THE NAME IS DELIBERATELY DIFFERENT, and this is a safety matter rather than a
style one. deploy_tool resolves by NAME and PUTs to whatever it resolves to.
Naming this `Get Table Trust Flags` would aim a full-replace PUT at that
existing tool — and the tool_type guard added on 2026-09-03 would NOT fire,
because both are `http` rather than one being a base tool. The 400 that saved
us from overwriting `List Critical Data Elements` would not come. Do not rename
this to match theirs.
GENERIC BY otype, deliberately. The endpoint takes any subject — data source,
schema, table, column, and also filters, joins and queries. The existing tenant
tool is table-only; flags exist at column level too, and a column-level
deprecation is the more precise signal when one column of a good table is bad.
include_propagated MATTERS AND DEFAULTS TO FALSE. A flag set on a schema
propagates to its tables, but the API will not return it unless asked, and the
existing tenant tool does not expose the parameter at all. So `deprecate the
legacy schema once` silently fails to reach the tables underneath. Send true
and read `is_propagated` to tell an inherited flag from a direct one.
TWO CALLS, NOT ONE. Search Catalog returns a COLUMN id, which is what
source_key needs; this wants the CONTAINING TABLE's id. The agent has to
resolve the table first — it already does this, having read table 664's
BCBS239_ELEMENT tag unprompted in earlier runs — but the prompt must say so
rather than assume the id is to hand.
AUTH VERIFIED BY EXECUTION 2026-09-08. The OAuth bearer DOES reach
/integration/flag/, despite the path carrying no v1 segment and the published
doc showing only the legacy TOKEN header. Test tool against oid=664,
otype=table returned HTTP 200 with []. A 200 with an empty body is the proof:
authenticated, reached the handler, and that table simply carries no flags.
Same shape of evidence as the /cde-service/ bearer finding — the response code
settles it where the documentation did not.
NO limit OR skip PARAMETER. The original reason given for this was WRONG and
is corrected here rather than quietly dropped: I predicted that Test tool's
pre-filled `limit: 0` would suppress results and make a flagged object read as
clean. It does not — the 2026-09-08 run against table 657 sent limit:0 and the
DEPRECATION came back regardless, so this endpoint treats 0 as unset. The
parameters are still omitted, for the plainer reason that an object carries a
handful of flags at most and pagination on a governance check can only ever
hide one. Do not add them back to rely on limit:0 being ignored — that is
undefined behaviour we happened to observe once.
flag_reason COMES BACK AS HTML, not text — and as WYSIWYG editor output, so a
reason typed in the UI arrives wrapped in
rgb(13,19,34); font-family: Inter...'> with a full inline style block. The
readable sentence is in there but a caller that quotes the field verbatim will
quote the styling with it. Anything presenting this to a human must take the
text content, and anything writing it into a CDE description — itself HTML —
must not nest the markup.
is_propagated IS ABSENT FROM THE RESPONSE ON THIS INSTANCE, though the
published spec documents it and we sent include_propagated=true. Observed keys
were id, flag_type, flag_reason, ts_created, ts_updated, subject, user. So a
flag inherited from a parent cannot be told from one set directly on the
object here. Keep sending include_propagated — a missing inherited flag is the
worse failure — but do not build logic that branches on is_propagated without
checking it exists first.
WHAT THE ANSWER MEANS. DEPRECATION is binding: do not attach the object, and
say why, quoting flag_reason. WARNING is not a veto — surface it in the
proposal and let the human decide. ENDORSEMENT is positive evidence that a
column is the authoritative one, which is exactly the control_point judgement.
Note that in Alation itself flags are ADVISORY — they colour a page and
penalise search rank, they do not block anything. Treating one as binding is a
choice this solution makes, and it should be described that way rather than as
a product behaviour.
name: Fetch Trust Flags
description: Read the trust flags on a catalog object — endorsements, warnings and deprecations — before relying on it. Returns flag_type (ENDORSEMENT, DEPRECATION, WARNING), the mandatory flag_reason explaining why, who set it, and whether it was inherited from a parent object. Call this on the table containing a column before attaching that column to a governed element: a DEPRECATION means the catalog has declared the object unfit for reporting, and attaching it would assert a lineage the catalog says does not hold. A WARNING is not a veto — report it and let a human judge. An ENDORSEMENT is evidence the object is the authoritative one. Note the id required here is the containing TABLE's id, not the column id returned by catalog search.

oid.description: Numeric id of the object to read flags for. For a table this is the TABLE id, not the id of a column inside it — catalog search returns column ids, so resolve the containing table first.

otype.description: Type of the object named by oid. Use 'table' when checking whether a table is fit to attach columns from, 'column' for a single column, 'schema' or 'data' for whole schemas and data sources. Must be sent together with oid.

include_propagated.description: Set true. A flag set on a parent — a schema deprecated as a whole — is NOT returned unless this is on, so leaving it off makes an inherited deprecation invisible and the object look clean. Each returned flag carries is_propagated so an inherited flag can be told from one set directly on this object.

exclude_deleted.description: Filter out flags whose subject has been deleted from the catalog.
